{{Short description|Iranian-American mathematician}}
'''Amir Mohammadi''' is an Iranian-American [[mathematician]] and professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="Berkeley">{{cite web |title=Amir Mohammadi |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~amirmo/ |website=UC Berkeley Department of Mathematics |access-date=6 October 2025}}</ref> His research focuses on [[Dynamical system#Construction of dynamical systems|homogeneous dynamics]], [[ergodic theory]], and [[number theory]].

== Career ==
Mohammadi earned his [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] from [[Sharif University of Technology]] in 2002 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Yale University]] in 2009.<ref name="Berkeley" /> He has held academic positions at the [[University of Chicago]], the [[University of Texas at Austin]], and [[University of California, San Diego|UC San Diego]] before joining the University of California, Berkeley, in 2025.<ref name="Berkeley" />

He was a [[von Neumann Fellowship|von Neumann Fellow]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] during 2015–2016.<ref name="IAS">{{cite web |title=Amir Mohammadi – Scholars profile |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/amir-mohammadi |website=Institute for Advanced Study |access-date=6 October 2025}}</ref>

== Research ==
Mohammadi’s research is primarily in homogeneous dynamics and [[ergodic theory]], with connections to [[arithmetic group]]s and [[Diophantine approximation]]. He has contributed to results on orbit closures, equidistribution, and measure classification, including work on the [[Oppenheim conjecture]] and effective methods in homogeneous spaces.<ref name="JAMS2020">{{cite journal |last1=Einsiedler |first1=Manfred |last2=Margulis |first2=Gregory |last3=Venkatesh |first3=Akshay |last4=Mohammadi |first4=Amir |title=Effective equidistribution and property (τ) |journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society |year=2020 |volume=33 |issue=4 |pages=1147–1203 |doi=10.1090/jams/951 |hdl=21.11116/0000-0008-021D-6 |arxiv=1809.01714 }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* [[Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems|Brin Prize]] in Dynamical Systems (2024)<ref name="BrinPrize">{{cite web |title=Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems – Past Laureates |url=https://science.psu.edu/math/research/dynsys/brinprize |website=Pennsylvania State University |access-date=6 October 2025}}</ref>
* Invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (2022)<ref name="ICM2022">{{cite web |title=International Congress of Mathematicians 2022 – Invited Speakers list |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=&order=field_speakers_congress_year&page=5&sort=desc |website=International Mathematical Union |access-date=6 October 2025}}</ref>
* [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] (2014–2016)<ref name="Sloan">{{cite web |title=2014 Sloan Research Fellowship recipients |url=https://web.mit.edu/dincalab/docs/NewYorkTimes_2014SloanResearchFellowships.pdf |website=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |access-date=6 October 2025}}</ref>
* [[von Neumann Fellowship]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (2015–2016)<ref name="IAS" />
